paper.title: PAC-Bayesian Lifelong Learning For Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Lifelong multi-armed bandits (tasks sampled i.i.d. from a task environment)
unmapped: Lifelong / meta-learning over a sequence of n MAB tasks, each with m rounds, tasks drawn i.i.d. from an unknown task environment (bayesian_prior used to express the task distribution)
Objective is a PAC-Bayesian lower bound on the marginal transfer reward (expected average reward over m rounds on a new task using a prior sampled from a hyperposterior), not regret
Guarantee is relative to an observable empirical importance-weighted multi-task reward
settings.definition_quote: We represent a multi-armed bandit (MAB) task as a couple T_i = (\mathcal{A}, \rho_i), where \mathcal{A} is a finite set of actions and \rho_i(r|a) is a distribution over rewards r that is conditioned on the action a. We assume that rewards are always between 0 and 1 and that tasks are sampled i.i.d. from an environment \mathcal{T}.

bound.expression: (1/lambda_1 + 1/(n_tasks*lambda_2))*KL_hyper + KL_post_sum/(n_tasks*m_task*lambda_2) + c_n + lambda_1/(8*n_tasks) + lambda_2*(E - 2)/(b_min*m_task) + log(2/delta)/lambda_1 + log(2*m_task/delta)/(n_tasks*lambda_2)

symbols.m_task: number of rounds per task m
symbols.lambda_2: free parameter lambda_2 in [0, m b_min]
symbols.KL_hyper: KL divergence between hyperposterior Q and hyperprior P
symbols.c_n: term measuring dependence of expected reward on past data (defined in Lemma 3)
symbols.b_min: minimum behaviour-policy probability over all tasks, rounds and actions

conditions: assumption (1): marginal expected reward of task n+k is at least that of task n for all priors P and j
hyperprior chosen before observing any task
tuning: holds simultaneously for all hyperposteriors Q

source.label: thm:big_bound_bern
source.quote: If condition (\ref{eqn:const_exp_assump}) is satisfied, then for any hyperprior $\mathcal{P}$, any $\lambda_1 > 0$, any $\lambda_2 \in [0, mb_{\mathrm{min}}]$ and any $\delta \in (0, 1]$, inequality (\ref{eqn:main_bern_lower}) holds with probability at least $1 - \delta$ over the tasks and their training sets ... and for all hyperposteriors $\mathcal{Q}$

results.notes: Recorded as an upper bound on the deficit Rhat(Q) - R(Q) between the empirical importance-weighted multi-task reward and the marginal transfer reward (paper states it as a lower bound on R(Q)). Holds for any hyperposterior / base learner, not a specific algorithm; used as objective by PAC-Bayes VI/MCMC (with epsilon-soft behaviour, b_min >= eps/K). Combines Lemma 3 and Lemma 6. Paper notes with lambda_1 ~ sqrt(n), lambda_2 ~ sqrt(m) the gap is O(1/sqrt(n) + 1/sqrt(m) + ...) ignoring c_n.

bound.expression: (1/lambda_1 + 1/(n_tasks*lambda_2))*KL_hyper + KL_post_sum/(n_tasks*m_task*lambda_2) + c_n + lambda_1/(8*n_tasks) + lambda_2*(1 + tau)**2/(8*m_task) + log(2/delta)/lambda_1 + log(2*m_task/delta)/(n_tasks*lambda_2)

symbols.KL_hyper: KL divergence between hyperposterior Q and hyperprior P
symbols.c_n: term measuring dependence of expected reward on past data (defined in Lemma 3)

cited_results.cited_title: PAC-Bayes-Bernstein inequality for martingales and its application to multiarmed bandits
cited_results.setting_description: Single stochastic K-armed bandit with rewards in [0,1], adaptive sampling distributions bounded below by eps_m; PAC-Bayes-Bernstein bound on R(Q_m) - Rhat(Q_m) for all m simultaneously w.p. 1-delta
